subject: Urgent: Montclair v5 rollout — error surge and p99 latency tail affecting checkout flows
messages:
From: Andrew Cho <andrew@montclair.ai>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: Montclair CS Ops <cs-ops@montclair.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: High error rate + p99 tail after v5 rollout (Montclair checkout)

Kimberly —

Quick heads up: we pushed Montclair v5 (quant profile v5a) to production at 07:40 PT and in the last 75 minutes we've seen a sharp uptick in 5xx errors and a p99 latency tail from ~220ms to ~1.9s on our payment checkout path. Users are reporting timeouts and abandoned carts.

Attached are the initial error logs and a perf dump. Key details:
- Error spike started ~08:02 PT, error rate peaked at 6.8% for the checkout endpoint.
- CPU on our side is nominal; the calls to Redwood show high decode time and increased tokenization CPU on your side per our traces.
- We temporarily rolled traffic to the v4.9 variant and errors dropped back to ~0.6%.

We're opening an incident (JIRA-INC-5278) but need urgent support — this is impacting revenue. Can your team confirm whether any quant-profile or kernel change in v5a could cause decode/connect latency increases? We can keep traffic on v4.9 if you recommend a rollback, but want your guidance.

Thanks,
Andrew
Head of Platform, Montclair AI

Attachments: perf_dump_2028-04-10.zip, errlog_2028-04-10.txt

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: Andrew Cho <andrew@montclair.ai>, Montclair CS Ops <cs-ops@montclair.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 09:35:12 -0700
Subject: Re: High error rate + p99 tail after v5 rollout (Montclair checkout)

Thanks Andrew — and sorry for the outage. I'm escalating internally and routing this to the infra/quant team for immediate triage.

Rishi / Priyom / Marissa — Montclair reports a sharp p99 tail and 5xx spike after the v5a quant rollout. They temporarily shifted traffic back to v4.9 with improvement. Andrew attached a perf dump and error log (see JIRA-INC-5278 and Drive link below).

Please do the following as priority:
1) Confirm whether v5a introduced any new kernel paths, attention changes, or kvcache layout changes that could increase per-request decode time.
2) Produce a short timeline of any infra or runtime changes tied to v5 release (commit ids/build tags).
3) If a fast rollback to v4.9 is the safe mitigation, advise estimated time-to-rollback and customer impact.
4) Propose an immediate mitigation (e.g., route Montclair to v4.9 automatically, reduce batch window, or temporarily disable the new quant profile).

I will coordinate the bridge with Andrew and loop in sales leadership if we need credits/SLA remediation.

Kimberly Park
Senior Director, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415 555 0192

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: Andrew Cho <andrew@montclair.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 10:05:47 -0700
Subject: Re: High error rate + p99 tail after v5 rollout (Montclair checkout)

Quick triage notes — preliminary but actionable:
- Root cause (probable): quant profile v5a introduced a micro-change in the decoder kernel ordering that increased per-token memory bandwidth and forced a fallback path on some older GPU SKUs, increasing decode time for longer sequences. Our perf traces show a 6-8x increase in token decode time for the longest tail buckets compared to v4.9 on identical inputs.
- Evidence: perf_dump shows repeated kernel fallback at step 3 (decode_loop) for requests > 120 tokens; errlog shows timeouts correlating to those requests.
- Impact: Montclair's checkout uses longer contexts for user prompts; their tail is exposed. Short-form calls (<64 tokens) unaffected.

Immediate mitigation options:
A) Roll traffic back to v4.9 (fastest, low-risk). Estimated time to rollback and propagate: ~15-25 minutes assuming we flip routing and warm caches.
B) Apply an emergency qprofile patch (v5a-1) reverting the kernel reorder — requires a controlled rollout and smoke tests, ETA ~90 minutes.
C) Route Montclair to a compatibility path that enforces a smaller max_tokens/batch limit to keep requests in the fast path — ETA ~30 minutes but may degrade throughput slightly.

Recommendation: authorize immediate rollback to v4.9 during peak hours so Montclair's revenue ops are protected, then follow with v5a-1 patch and controlled canary. If leadership prefers to avoid rollback, we can implement C as a temporary stopgap.

Attachments: perf_dump_2028-04-10.zip (uploaded to incident), sample kernel trace excerpt pasted into JIRA-INC-5278.

Rishi Malhotra
Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 11 Apr 2028 08:15:03 -0700
Subject: Montclair v5 rollback recommendation + exec summary

Andrew / Execs —

Short summary and ask: Rishi's team recommends an immediate rollback for Montclair from v5a to v4.9 (Option A) to eliminate the p99 latency tail and 5xx spike affecting their checkout flow. The rollback is low-risk and estimated to complete within 15-25 minutes once we flip routing and warm caches.

Why: preliminary traces show v5a triggers a decoder kernel fallback for the longest sequences on certain GPU SKUs which increases per-token decode time and surfaces as high p99. Montclair's checkout uses longer contexts and is sensitive to the tail. Traffic rolled back on Montclair's side to v4.9 showed error rates fall from 6.8% to ~0.6% immediately.

Customer impact: revenue-sensitive checkout path; Montclair has paused promotions and is experiencing measurable abandonment. They have requested a rollback and SLA credit evaluation if rollout caused sustained business impact.

Proposed immediate actions (ask for sign-off):
- Approve emergency rollback to v4.9 for Montclair (I will coordinate with Rishi/Priyom).
- Offer Montclair a one-time credit equal to 10% of last month's usage during the outage window as good faith (sales to finalize).
- Post-rollback: run v5a-1 (patched) in canary for 24 hours and coordinate a slow re-roll with performance smoke tests.

Requested approval: Kimberly Park (Customer Success) requests a go/no-go for the rollback within 20 minutes to avoid further revenue loss.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Director, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415 555 0192
